summary: Troopers arrested a Fairbanks woman on Oct. 26 on domestic violence assault charges and two counts of assault in the presence of a child. Seven criminal cases were filed at the Fairbanks courthouse on Oct. 26, three of them carrying a felony count, and two older cases appeared in the database the same day. Two of those cases closed on Oct. 26 and can no longer be found in the state's online case database, although the court's weekly report still lists them. No new charge was filed in the Interior overnight. The Alaska Court System's weekly report for Oct. 20 to 26 lists 50 new criminal cases at Fairbanks and one at Nenana, and prints no section for Healy or Delta Junction, which records that those courts had no filings in that week rather than that their records were examined.

entries.title: DV assault arrest: Billie Foltz
body: Billie Foltz, 41, of Fairbanks was arrested on Oct. 26 on domestic violence assault charges and two counts of assault in the presence of a child. Fourth-degree assault means recklessly causing injury to another person; no charge classification has been filed yet.
Troopers say a man reported that his partner had assaulted him between about midnight and 1 a.m. that day, and that the report reached them at about 7:38 p.m. Alaska State Troopers case AK26106268.
No court case has been opened. A search of the state case database on Oct. 27 returned no Fairbanks criminal file under the name.

entries.title: Indecent exposure charges: Samuel Jasiel Benjamin Malone
body: Samuel Jasiel Benjamin Malone, 30, is charged in two separate cases with first-degree indecent exposure with a prior conviction, a Class C felony, punishable by up to five years.

According to Fairbanks Police, he was arrested at the 2400 block of Bjerremark Street at Twenty-Fifth Avenue at 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 25, and again at the 100 block of Airport Way at Peger Road at 8:12 p.m. the same day.
The first case also charges second-degree stalking, a course of conduct placing another person in fear, a Class A misdemeanor. The second adds violating a condition of release, a Class B misdemeanor.
Cases 4FA-26-02167CR and 4FA-26-02169CR; preliminary hearings Nov. 5 and Nov. 12.

entries.title: Felony theft charge: Dustin Edward Walters
body: Dustin Edward Walters is charged with second-degree theft, taking property worth $750 to $24,999, a Class C felony punishable by up to five years.
He is also charged with violating a condition of release, a Class B misdemeanor, and cited for driving with a revoked license. The charges are dated Oct. 25 at Fairbanks.
Case 4FA-26-02166CR; preliminary hearings Nov. 5 and Nov. 12.

entries.title: DV assault charges: Thomas James Madison Grover
body: Thomas James Madison Grover is charged with fourth-degree assault, recklessly causing injury, and with assault committed when a child is present. Both are Class A misdemeanors recorded as domestic violence.
The charges are dated Oct. 25 at Fairbanks. Case 4FA-26-02168CR; pre-trial conference Dec. 24 and a trial week set for Dec. 7.

entries.title: Theft charge: William Howard Frasure
body: William Howard Frasure, 36, is charged with third-degree theft, taking property worth $250 to $749, a Class A misdemeanor.
According to Fairbanks Police, he was arrested at the 100 block of Illinois Street at Phillips Field Road at 1:43 p.m. on Oct. 24.
Case 4FA-26-02170CR; pre-trial conference Dec. 17.

entries.title: False-name traffic stop arrest: Nicole Noelle Thompson
body: Nicole Noelle Thompson was arrested on Oct. 26 on an outstanding warrant and additional charges after troopers say she twice gave another woman's name at traffic stops.

Troopers say she was stopped for speeding near Johansen Expressway and University Avenue at about 2:15 a.m. on Oct. 25, and stopped again in the same area at about 6:25 a.m. on Oct. 26 after an illegal U-turn.
Case 4FA-26-02163CR, where no charging document has been filed yet; arraignment Nov. 3.

entries.title: DV assault charge and warrant: Tatyana May Alayzia Bet Ashely-Moore
body: Tatyana May Alayzia Bet Ashely-Moore is charged with fourth-degree assault, recklessly causing injury, a Class A misdemeanor recorded as domestic violence. The charge is dated Oct. 11 at Fairbanks and the case was filed Oct. 23.
The court issued a warrant for her arrest on Oct. 26 with a $500 unsecured appearance bond. No hearing is set. Case 4FA-26-02164CR.

entries.title: Case dismissed for lack of probable cause: Jess Lee Antonich Eakin
body: A criminal case filed against Jess Lee Antonich Eakin on Oct. 23 was dismissed on Oct. 26 on a finding of no probable cause, and the case was closed the same day.

The case charged unlawful contact in breach of a court order, contacting someone a court order forbids contacting, a Class A misdemeanor recorded as domestic violence, and violating a condition of release, a Class B misdemeanor. Both charges were dated Oct. 22 at Fairbanks.
Case 4FA-26-02165CR. The case is listed in the Alaska Court System's weekly charges report but no longer appears in the state's online case database.

sources.label: Alaska Court System weekly charges report

entries.title: Two Fairbanks cases closed Monday can no longer be looked up online
body: Two criminal cases at the Fairbanks courthouse that closed on Oct. 26 can no longer be found in the Alaska Court System's public case database, by case number or by party name.

Case 4FA-26-02165CR, filed Oct. 23, was dismissed for lack of probable cause. Case 4FA-26-02171CR, filed the same day it closed, against Michael Wright-Germany, was closed with a docket entry reading that no complaint or citation had been filed.

Both case numbers are printed in the court system's weekly charges report for Oct. 20 to 26, which was produced at 9:01 p.m. on Oct. 26, after both cases closed. The seven other cases filed at Fairbanks that day can still be looked up.
